# Deadzone Rogue

## What does randomization do to this game?

The unlocks you normally earn by completing missions are shuffled into the multiworld. Completing missions
sends checks out to other players instead. What you receive:

- **Weapons, perk families and augments**, one item each. By default, the ones that are normally free from the
  start are shuffled too. The client locks them until you receive them, and you begin with a small random
  starting kit so the first runs are playable.
- **Item Packs, Mastery Packs and Superior Item Packs**: the run items, Tech upgrades and SuperItem upgrades,
  dealt out in random packs (pack size is an option). Mastery and Superior Item Packs come in several copies: each
  copy raises every upgrade in the pack by a few levels (an option), so you find them more than once. Those
  upgrades can't be bought at the station; only other players' checks level them up.
- **Unlocks**: the "Fate" rerolls, Fabricator restocks, Tier 10 Tech Upgrades and Epic Beginnings.
- **Zone Access** (optional), which unlocks zones 2–4. A zone's first story mission opens as soon as its access arrives, even if earlier zones' story missions aren't done. Difficulties are never locked; each one is just a separate check.

## What counts as a location check?

- Completing each mission on each difficulty you enable, as separate checks, for example
  "Who am I? (Adventure)", "Who am I? (Normal)", "Who am I? (Hard)". Story and challenge missions both count.
- Save-wide objectives, counted across every run on your Archipelago save: sectors cleared, enemies killed and
  Scrap gathered, for example "Sectors Cleared: 10", "Enemies Killed: 300", "Scrap Gathered: 2000". The totals
  and intervals are options.

## What is the goal?

Complete every story and challenge mission in zones 1 through 4 (or through 3, for a shorter game), on
any difficulty. The endless-wave missions (Gauntlet, Crossfire, Last Stand) don't count. Type `/goal` in the client
to see what's left.

## DeathLink

When another player dies, your current run isn't ended by default. Instead you lose a random perk, depending on
`death_link_mode`. Other modes are losing an item, losing half your Scrap, dropping to a quarter of your health, or a
real death. Only what you picked up during the run can be lost, never your unlocks. Deaths that arrive while you're
in the hub are skipped.

## What does another world's item look like in Deadzone Rogue?

A line in the in-game chat, prefixed `[Archipelago]`, names the item and the player it was sent to.

tutorials.text:
# Deadzone Rogue Setup Guide

## Required software

- Deadzone: Rogue (Steam, PC)
- [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases) 0.6.6 or newer
- [UE4SS](https://github.com/UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS/releases) experimental build (the `UE4SS_v3.0.1-…zip` from
  "experimental-latest"). The 3.0.1 stable release doesn't support the game's Unreal version.
- From this project's [releases](https://github.com/CaptCapybara-cmd/Archipelago-DeadzoneRogue/releases):
  `deadzone_rogue.apworld` and `APClient-<version>.zip`

## Installing with the launcher (easiest)

Download `DeadzoneRogueLauncher.exe` from the releases and run it. Windows may warn that it's from an unknown
publisher, because the launcher isn't code-signed; choose "More info", then "Run anyway".

- **Setup tab:** it finds the game through Steam. **Install / update mod** downloads UE4SS from its official GitHub
  release (checking the file's SHA-256), then adds the crash fix and the APClient mod. **Install world into
  Archipelago** adds the world to your Archipelago install.
- **Options tab:** pick your options and save your YAML.
- **Play tab:** start the client and the game, and check that everything is ready.

## Installing by hand

1. **UE4SS:** extract the UE4SS zip into `Steam\steamapps\common\Deadzone Rogue\Valhalla\Binaries\Win64`, so that
   `dwmapi.dll` and the `ue4ss` folder sit next to `DeadzoneSteam-Win64-Shipping.exe`.
2. **APClient:** extract `APClient-<version>.zip` into the same `Win64` folder. It adds
   `ue4ss\VTableLayout.ini` (without it, UE4SS crashes this game on startup) and the `ue4ss\Mods\APClient` mod,
   which is enabled automatically by its `enabled.txt`.
3. **World:** double-click `deadzone_rogue.apworld`, or put it in Archipelago's `custom_worlds` folder.

## Save slots

Archipelago changes your unlocks. Start a **new save slot** in the game's save menu for each multiworld, and keep
your normal progress in another slot.

The first save slot you play while the client is connected becomes that multiworld's slot. On every other slot
the mod does nothing: no items, no locks, no checks. That keeps your normal saves safe even with the client running.

## Creating a YAML

Use the launcher's Options tab, Archipelago's "Options Creator", or start from `Deadzone Rogue.yaml`, and send the
result to your host.

## Connecting

1. Open the Archipelago Launcher and start **Deadzone Rogue Client**. Connect with the room's address and your
   slot name.
   - If the game isn't in the default Steam folder, run `/gamedir <path to Valhalla\Binaries\Win64>`.
2. Start the game and pick your Archipelago save slot. `/game` in the client tells you whether the mod is
   talking to it.
3. Received items are granted within a second or two of arriving. Normally-free content you haven't received
   yet is locked.
4. The mod posts to the in-game chat, prefixed `[Archipelago]`: when it loads, when your save slot connects, and
   for every item you send or receive. Press **F10** in game for a status line (mod version, save slot, open zones).

readme.text:
# Deadzone Rogue – Archipelago

An Archipelago integration has two halves:

| Half | What it does | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **APWorld** (`deadzone_rogue/`, Python) | Tells the generator what items and locations exist and what the logic is | v0.8.2: built from the game's real data, passes AP's tests, generates seeds |
| **Client** (Python, in the apworld) + **APClient** (Lua mod) | Talks to the AP server: sends checks, grants received items, locks unreceived content, reports the goal | v0.8.2: mission and save-wide objective checks, grants, locking and zone gating work live, protected by save-slot binding. DeathLink effects work in a run; the game's own mission rewards for shuffled unlocks are taken back |

## Files

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [Releases](https://github.com/CaptCapybara-cmd/Archipelago-DeadzoneRogue/releases) | **`DeadzoneRogueLauncher.exe`** (installs everything and builds your YAML), `deadzone_rogue.apworld` (world + client), `APClient-<version>.zip` (in-game mod + UE4SS crash fix) and the template YAML. Install steps: [setup guide](deadzone_rogue/docs/setup_en.md) |
| [Deadzone Rogue.yaml](Deadzone%20Rogue.yaml) | Template player options, to fill in and give to the host |
| `deadzone_rogue/` | World source. `game_data.py` is generated; don't edit it by hand |
| `tools/gen_data.py` | Rebuilds `game_data.py` and `client/ap_data.json` from `dumps/APCatalog.tsv` |
| `client/ap_data.json` | For the client mod: AP id → asset paths to grant or lock, mission GUIDs, pack pools |
| `launcher/` | The launcher (Python + tkinter). `tools/build_launcher.py` packages it with PyInstaller; `tools/export_options.py` regenerates its options form from the world |
| `ue4ss_setup/` | UE4SS crash fix (`VTableLayout.ini`), the catalog/dump/test Lua mods, and the windowed launch script |
| `dumps/` | Header dump, object dump, `.usmap`, asset catalog, hook test log |
| [HOOKS.md](HOOKS.md) | What's verified in-game and how |

## The game, technically

- **Unreal Engine 5.6.1** (internal project name `Valhalla`), game version 1.4.2, by Prophecy Games. No anti-cheat.
- UE4SS needs `ue4ss_setup/VTableLayout.ini` to start (it fixes [UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS#1048](https://github.com/UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS/issues/1048)).
- Saves are local: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Valhalla\Saved\SaveGames`, one file per slot. Use a separate slot for AP.

## The APWorld

**Checks**
- Each mission × each difficulty in `mission_difficulties` (Adventure/Normal/Hard by default, up to 5 levels).
  There are 32 missions: 6 story and 26 challenge, across 4 zones.
- Save-wide objectives, counted across every run on your Archipelago save: **Sectors Cleared**, **Enemies Killed**
  (your own kills) and **Scrap Gathered** (pickups; spending doesn't count). Each has a total and an interval
  option, for example a check every 300 kills up to 3000. Total 0 turns one off.
- Endless-wave missions (Gauntlet, Crossfire, Last Stand) only have checks with `include_endless_missions`.

**Items**
- Weapons, perk families and augments as individual items. `*_shuffle` is `none` / `locked_only` / `all`; `all` also
  locks the normally-free ones and gives a starting kit.
- Item / Mastery (Tech upgrade) / Superior Item (SuperItem upgrade) **packs**: random groups per seed, with
  `*_pack_size` options (0 = off). The pack contents go to the client in slot data.
- Mastery and Superior Item packs are **progressive**: every copy raises the pack's upgrades by
  `tech_levels_per_copy` / `superior_levels_per_copy` levels (the first copy also unlocks them), and while they're
  shuffled those upgrades can't be bought in the hub. Tier 10 Tech Upgrades is left out then.
- Unlocks: the Fate rerolls, Fabricator restocks (two progressive chains), Tier 10 Tech Upgrades, Epic Beginnings.
- Optional `Zone N Access` items (zone gating). Difficulties are never gated; each is just a separate check. Zone Access opens that zone's first story mission even when the earlier story isn't done; after that, logic follows the game's own mission prerequisites.
- If there are more items than checks, the lowest-priority items are left out (they stay as in the base game):
  synergies, then packs, unlocks, augments, weapons, perks.

**Goal:** complete every story and challenge mission in zones 1 through the chosen zone (`goal: zone_3` or `zone_4`),
on any difficulty. Endless-wave missions never count. A challenge that only exists on one difficulty counts only if
that difficulty has checks. `/goal` in the client lists what's left.

**DeathLink:** `death_link_mode` = lose_perk (default) / lose_item / lose_scrap / take_damage / kill.

### Rebuilding

1. Clone https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago and copy `deadzone_rogue/` into `worlds/`.
2. `pip install -r requirements.txt`
3. If the game updates: rerun the APCatalog mod **with APClient disabled** (its locks would otherwise be recorded as
   the game's defaults), copy the new `APCatalog.tsv` into `dumps/`, then run `python tools/gen_data.py`.
   **Check the item ids it prints. Ids must never change once seeds exist.**
4. Tests: `python -m pytest worlds/deadzone_rogue test/general`
5. Build: `python Launcher.py "Build APWorlds" -- "Deadzone Rogue"`

## The client

- **Deadzone Rogue Client** (`deadzone_rogue/client.py`) shows up in the Archipelago Launcher. It connects to the
  server and exchanges plain-text files with the game in `Win64/APBridge/` (format in `deadzone_rogue/bridge.py`).
- **APClient** (`ue4ss_setup/Mods/APClient`) is the in-game half: hooks for checks, `AddInventoryCount` grants,
  `bRequireOwnership` locks, and per-session/per-save-slot state.
- Install steps for players: `deadzone_rogue/docs/setup_en.md`. What's done and what's left:
  [HOOKS.md](HOOKS.md#client-to-do).

## Roadmap

- **DeathLink with another player**: every effect is verified in game; a death arriving from (and sent to)
  another game hasn't been tried yet.

## AI use

Much of this project's code and documentation was written with Claude, an AI assistant made by Anthropic. The
maintainer directed the work, decided how it should behave, and tested it in the game. Commits made with AI help
carry a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` line.

## Credits

- [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago) (MIT): the multiworld framework this world and client
  are built on.
- [RE-UE4SS](https://github.com/UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS) (MIT): the Lua modding framework the APClient mod runs on. The
  launcher downloads the official release from its GitHub page; it isn't bundled here.
- [PyInstaller](https://pyinstaller.org) packages the launcher as a single exe.

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Deadzone: Rogue belongs to Prophecy Games; this project ships no game files.

notes.text:
Two crash fixes. Update both the world and the mod: they're versioned as a pair.

## Fixed
- **Game crash when an enemy died without a killer.** The kill counter read the killer of every enemy that died; an enemy killed by a hazard, an explosion or another enemy has none, and that crashed the game. Those kills are now skipped. Your own kills still count.
- **Client lost its server connection after receiving an item.** Windows sometimes refused to update the file the client shares with the mod, if the mod happened to be reading it at that moment (`[WinError 5] Access is denied … inbox.txt`). That error dropped the connection. The client now retries for a moment, and if it still can't write, it keeps the connection and tries again a second later.

## Downloads
- **`DeadzoneRogueLauncher.exe`**: installs UE4SS, the crash fix and the APClient mod into the game, installs the world into Archipelago, and builds your YAML. Windows may warn about an unknown publisher, because the launcher isn't code-signed; choose *More info* → *Run anyway*.
- **`deadzone_rogue.apworld`**: the world, plus the **Deadzone Rogue Client**, which appears in the Archipelago Launcher.
- **`APClient-v0.8.2.zip`**: the in-game mod and the UE4SS crash fix, for installing by hand. Extract it into `Deadzone Rogue\Valhalla\Binaries\Win64`.
- **`Deadzone Rogue.yaml`**: template player options. Nothing changed since v0.8.1.

To update, use the launcher's **Install / update mod** and **Install world into Archipelago** buttons, then restart the Deadzone Rogue Client and the game.

See the [setup guide](https://github.com/CaptCapybara-cmd/Archipelago-DeadzoneRogue/blob/main/deadzone_rogue/docs/setup_en.md).
